evidence: Cic. Man. 17: vectīgālia nervōs esse reī pūblicae
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a toll, tax, impost paid to the State. To impose a tax is vectīgal impōnere (with the dative), to collect taxes vectīgālia exigere, to pay them vectīgālia pēnsitāre (Cic. Man. 16; Traupman 390); a tax collector is exāctor (Traupman 169, 390). Tax-free is vectīgālium immūnis (M-O).

terms.gloss: a direct tax, a levy; tribute
evidence: Caes. BG 6.14.1: neque tribūta ūnā cum reliquīs pendunt
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: a stated payment, a contribution, tribute: the levy on Roman citizens and the tribute of subject peoples. For customs duties see customs duty.

phrases.latin: vectīgālia nervōs esse reī pūblicae semper dūximus
phrases.english: we have always held taxes to be the sinews of the state

phrases.latin: Druidēs ā bellō abesse cōnsuērunt neque tribūta ūnā cum reliquīs pendunt
phrases.english: The druids usually stay out of war, and they do not pay taxes like everyone else

phrases.latin: Plērīque, cum aut aere aliēnō aut magnitūdine tribūtōrum aut injūriā potentiōrum premuntur, sēsē in servitūtem dicant nōbilibus
phrases.english: Most of them, when they are weighed down by debt, by heavy taxes or by the wrongs of the powerful, give themselves up as slaves to the nobles
